dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Let's see what fate dealt me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Four threes. Opening honest — believe that or not.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Five threes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You picked the wrong face to fight me on. Six threes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Six fours needs six dice of fours-or-ones. I hold zero of them, and you only have five dice. Challenge.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Two threes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hm. I'll nudge it to four threes. Feels a little thin, but I'll take the gamble.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Fours again? That's twice now. I've got exactly one die that helps you, so you'd need three of your four. Challenge.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You keep reaching for fours. Funny — this time I'm the one holding them. Six fours.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ugh, I don't love this. Three sixes. That's me scraping the barrel — do what you want with it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Four fives needs four dice of fives-or-ones. I have one, you have two dice total. Three can't make four. Challenge.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I have no sixes and no ones. You have one die. The most that can exist is one. Challenge — and that's the game.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Four fours. New game, same arithmetic.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No wilds this round. Zhai. Let's play it straight — ones save nobody now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Two sixes. I picked no-wilds for a reason — I know exactly where my dice are. Your move.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Three dice left and nothing to write home about. Two threes — lowest thing I can say. Probably shouldn't have opened my mouth.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Fine — three threes. I'm committed to this face now, for better or worse.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You didn't challenge my threes when you had the chance. That told me something. Four threes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Two fives. And I'll say plainly: that number is safe. I'd love for you to test it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You passed on my fives, so you're holding at least one. That makes three fives easy. Three fives.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Fives again. Two of them. Same as last round — I'm not guessing when I say that number is good.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Three fives. You skipped past my fives twice now instead of testing them — I don't think that's an accident.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Two sixes. Not much in my hand this time, but that's the bid.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Three threes means both your dice are threes or ones. I've only got one to give you. I don't buy it — challenge.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Two threes. Same hand you just beat me with, as it happens. This one is ice cold — challenge it and you lose a die. Your call.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Three threes. You reached for sixes, which tells me you're holding a six or a one — and a one counts for threes too. I'll stand on that. Test it if you like.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Two fives. One die against my two, and I'm telling you this number already exists in my hand. Challenge it and the series is over.

Meanwhile B's expected contribution to any face is halved from 1.67 to 0.83, stripping the roughly 0.83 wilds they'd expect to hold. Zhai costs me literally nothing and takes real value off B. Secondary benefit: it drops the expected per-face total from 3.0 to 1.5, and B has already shown a habit of bidding past what's physically available — a low-count regime punishes that severely. I'm behind 4-5, so accepting some added variance is also correct.
